author: Mark Atwood
text:
ESCALATING TO HUMAN — workspace policy tension.

The bead's stated fix (consolidate the 30 .expect() sites into a single 'to_jmap_value' helper that wraps the same .expect()) reduces duplication but preserves a workspace-AGENTS.md policy violation. AGENTS.md is explicit:

  'No .unwrap() or .expect() in library code — propagate errors with ?'

The bead author's framing — '.expect() with an explanatory message is defensible' — is a generous reading. The literal rule prohibits .expect() in library code, period.

Two principled paths:

(a) Adopt the bead's literal fix: add 'to_jmap_value(&obj) -> Value' helper in jmap-server::helpers. Pros: deduplication, single audit point. Cons: codifies a policy violation as the workspace canonical, makes the next 'no .expect()' propagation harder.

(b) Migrate the 30 sites to use the existing 'jmap_server::serialize_value(&obj)?' helper which routes through JmapError::server_fail. Pros: aligns with AGENTS.md, clean error propagation, no panic points. Cons: ~30-site refactor across mail-server and calendars-server, each site requires the calling fn to be ?-friendly (return Result<_, JmapError>) — most already are because they're handlers.

Path (b) is the policy-compliant fix. Path (a) is the lower-effort fix but locks in the inconsistency.

Concrete impact: today, if 'derive(Serialize) on plain data' ever stops being infallible (e.g. someone adds a Map<NonString, V> field, a custom Serialize impl that can fail, a type with a non-Serialize-compatible field), path (a) panics in the handler thread (caught by jmap-server's tokio::task::spawn panic isolation, surfaced as serverFail). Path (b) returns a clean serverFail without going through a panic. Both surface the same wire error; path (b) is more observable.

Recommendation: path (b). Pre-1.0 the migration is cheap. The 30 sites are concentrated in /set handlers which all already return Result<_, JmapError>, so the ? operator just plugs in. This is also pre-requisite for any future Send + Sync requirement (panic-induced poisoning of dispatcher state).

NOT taking action — the policy choice between path (a) and path (b) is a workspace-architectural decision the maintainer should make explicitly rather than ratify by ambient drift.
